execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript in compromised subdomain web pages (HTML/JS files on attacker-controlled server)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
// Obfuscated JavaScript loaded from Russian-hosted server
(function(){var _0xabc=...; /* obfuscated code */ })();
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime (when a user visits the compromised subdomain), the code executes obfuscated JavaScript loaded from a Russian-hosted server, manipulates the DOM to hide or dynamically load site content, and potentially tracks or redirects users, resulting in user deception and possible credential or information theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated JavaScript loaded from an external, attacker-controlled server is a common technique for hiding malicious logic and evading detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate subdomain web pages should not load obfuscated scripts from untrusted, foreign servers, nor should they hide all content via CSS or dynamically load content in a deceptive manner.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation is sometimes used for intellectual property protection or to reduce code size, but not for critical web infrastructure or in combination with suspicious hosting.
key_indicators: External script source from Russian-hosted server
DOM manipulation to hide or dynamically load content

attack_chain.action: Threat actor discovers a DNS record pointing to a decommissioned AWS/Azure resource.
attack_chain.leads_to: Opportunity to claim the resource and control the subdomain.

attack_chain.action: Threat actor stands up an identical AWS/Azure resource and points DNS records to their own server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains control of the subdomain.

attack_chain.action: Attacker hosts spam or phishing sites on the compromised subdomain, injecting obfuscated JavaScript from Russian-hosted servers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious content is served to visitors, enabling user deception, tracking, or credential theft.

attack_chain.action: Attacker adapts site format and naming to evade detection, using randomly generated names and hiding content via CSS/dynamic loading.
attack_chain.leads_to: Increased persistence and reduced likelihood of detection.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated JavaScript loaded from external, non-corporate servers
All links on a page are self-referential or loop back to the same domain
Large numbers of dynamically generated pages (20,000+ sitemaps) in multiple languages
Content hidden via CSS or loaded dynamically
file_indicators: HTML/JS files with high entropy or obfuscated code
Sitemaps with tens of thousands of entries
network_indicators: Unusual script loads from non-corporate infrastructure
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor subdomains for unexpected DNS changes or new cloud resource associations. Scan web content for obfuscated JavaScript, especially scripts loaded from foreign or untrusted domains. Flag subdomains with self-referential links, excessive sitemaps, or content hidden via CSS/dynamic loading. Use attack surface management tools to inventory and continuously monitor all subdomains for unauthorized changes or suspicious content.
